Write the WAI measures behind the public dashboard

Source: R/web-export.R
export_wai_measures.Rd

Companion to export_wai_web(): from the same weekly fit, write the three measures the dashboard explains the indicator with, each on the scale the dashboard publishes, so that its charts add up to the numbers it shows. Written by analysis/update_wai_web.R; not package API.

Usage

export_wai_measures(
  fit_path,
  dir = NULL,
  series_info = NULL,
  news_fit_path = NULL,
  news_new_data = NULL,
  digits = 4,
  vintage_date = NULL
)

Arguments

fit_path

Path to this week's fit .Rda (object mod), as for export_wai_web().

dir

Directory to write into, or NULL to only return the tables.

series_info

Optional data frame with columns key, name and group; series it lacks keep their key as name and go into "Other".

news_fit_path

Optional path to LAST week's fit, the old vintage of the news decomposition.

news_new_data

Optional list with flows and stocks: this week's data, prepared exactly as this week's fit's was.

digits

Decimal places of the published values.

vintage_date

Optional vintage date recorded in the metadata.

Value

Invisibly, a list with contributions, series, news (or NULL) and meta.

Details

Contributions (wai_contributions.csv). mfbdfm_contributions() splits the factor exactly, but on the sampler's standardised, non-annualised scale. The published wai_qoq is F(z) = ((1 + sd*z + mean/k)^48 - 1) * 100 of that, which is not linear, so contributions to it do not exist as such. The file therefore uses an exact additive split on the published scale: trend = F(0) (the growth the model implies with every contribution at zero), each group's share of F(T) - F(0) in proportion to its standardised contribution (T the plug-in total), and parameter_uncertainty = wai_qoq - F(T), the posterior-minus-plug-in residual mfbdfm_contributions() itself reports. Per date the components sum to wai_qoq exactly.

News (wai_news.csv). mfbdfm_news() of the move from news_fit_path (last week's fit) to news_new_data (this week's data), aggregated to the groups and mapped onto annualised quarterly growth the same way: shares of G(new) - G(old), G(x) = ((1 + x)^4 - 1) * 100, which sum exactly to the revision. Written only when both arguments are given.

Series (wai_series.csv). One row per input series: name and group, frequency, the R-squared from summary() and the posterior loading with its 95% band (standardised scale, so loadings are comparable across series).

See also

export_wai_web(), mfbdfm_contributions(), mfbdfm_news().
